content.user_title: Map Skills to Clear Proficiency Levels
content.value_statement: Learning plans often use subjective levels that hide missing prerequisites and uneven progress. This skill applies CEFR, Bloom's Taxonomy, and DigComp to create measurable, connected skill progressions.
actual_capabilities: Maps skills to CEFR, Bloom's Taxonomy, and DigComp proficiency frameworks.
Defines measurable indicators for A1 through C2 skill levels.
Checks that prerequisite skills appear before dependent skills.
Identifies proficiency regression across lessons or chapters.
Suggests proficiency-matched assessment types and rubrics.
Applies five coherence checks for naming, progression, prerequisites, connectivity, and uniqueness.
limitations: It provides a reasoning framework, not independently verified learner measurements.
It does not replace subject matter experts or formal assessment validation.
CEFR mappings for non-language domains require local context and review.
It does not create course materials unless you provide the curriculum details.

use_cases.title: Plan a course progression
use_cases.description: Map chapter skills from beginner foundations to independent application without missing prerequisites.

use_cases.title: Review training consistency
use_cases.description: Find regressive levels, duplicate skill names, and isolated lessons in an existing training program.

use_cases.title: Design practical assessments
use_cases.description: Match recognition, application, analysis, and real-world tasks to the intended proficiency level.

prompt_templates.title: Map one skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the skill "write a basic project specification" to CEFR and Bloom levels. Give measurable indicators for A1, A2, and B1.

prompt_templates.title: Check lesson prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these lesson skills and levels: [paste list]. Identify missing prerequisites and any regression. Recommend a corrected sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Create assessment criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: For the B1 skill "debug a simple application independently," create measurable indicators, assessment tasks, and a proficiency-specific rubric.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a full curriculum
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this curriculum outline: [paste outline]. Apply CEFR, Bloom, and the five coherence tests. Return a progression map, issues, and prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Map the skill "use version control" from A1 to B1.
output: A1: Recognizes repositories, commits, and branches.
A2: Creates commits and switches branches with guidance.
B1: Resolves routine merge conflicts and uses branches independently.

output_examples.input: Check a sequence where an A2 lesson follows a B1 lesson on the same skill.
output_examples.output: Progression issue found: the later A2 lesson regresses from independent application. Raise its task to B1 or move it before the B1 lesson.

output_examples.input: Suggest an assessment for a B2 specification skill.
output_examples.output: Use a comparative design task where learners critique two specifications, explain tradeoffs, and recommend improvements with evidence.

best_practices: Provide the skill, learner background, available time, and intended outcome.
Use observable learner actions instead of labels such as easy or advanced.
Review progression and prerequisites whenever lessons change.
anti_patterns: Do not assign levels only because a task feels difficult.
Do not introduce dependent skills before their foundational skills.
Do not use the same assessment task for every proficiency level.

faq.question: What does this skill map?
faq.answer: It maps learning skills, lesson outcomes, and assessments to structured proficiency levels.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it use?
faq.answer: It uses CEFR, Bloom's Taxonomy, DigComp, and cognitive load principles.

faq.question: Can it review an existing curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the lesson sequence and skill levels for a coherence and progression review.

faq.question: Does it measure individual learner performance?
faq.answer: No. It designs and calibrates the framework. Human assessment evidence is still required.

faq.question: Is it limited to language education?
faq.answer: No. It adapts proficiency reasoning to professional, technical, and digital skills.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Share learner prerequisites, course sequence, target outcomes, available time, and existing assessment methods.
